decisions.reason: As a flagship harvesting crate aligned with the firm's reusable-packaging direction, it likely meets aspirations, and a large firm has the slack to carry it while agricultural adoption builds.
A multi-model foldable large container line with its own page fits the core automotive and industrial business and gives no shortfall signal that would trigger search for alternatives.
Stackable crates are a staple of the established portfolio, so the line plausibly performs at aspiration level, though its low prominence on the website adds slight uncertainty.
A medium-duty rackable pallet line complements the core pallet range, and with no evidence of underperformance the firm has no reason to redirect its resources.
The spill-retention pallet line serves a narrower niche that is somewhat further from the core logistics focus, but its own page and the firm's slack argue for keeping it.

This single-model pallet with load retainers is a more marginal variant at modest risk if results fall short, but a dedicated page and a short time on the market suggest the firm will keep it for now.
